title: Expectation Linter and Snapshot Summarizer CI Adapter
author: Rajiv Menon
description:
Context: We frequently see small, hard-to-explain regressions in prompt-set SLOs after model upgrades or tokenization changes. Existing CI smokechecks run raw metrics (accuracy, exact-match) but lack a lightweight, human-readable layer that encodes expectations over distributions and highlights where regressions are concentrated. This PR adds two orthogonal components: 1) an 'Expectation Linter' that validates metric distributions and token-level expectations for named prompt cohorts; and 2) a 'Snapshot Summarizer' adapter that produces compact summary artifacts consumed by CI gating logic and by the Console telemetry pipeline. The linter supports rule types (median shift, tail-regression, token-saliency drift, and categorical confusion delta) and emits structured warnings with source cohort, metric, and suggested remediation. The summarizer rolls per-cohort metrics into a deterministic compact snapshot (JSON + compressed CSV) that is archived as a CI artifact and used by the gating adapter to apply soft/hard fail policies. Design goals: minimal CI overhead (vectorized evaluation, incremental snapshot diffing), explainability (human-friendly summary table + provenance links), and actionable outputs (auto-suggest revert/rollforward candidates when available). Changes in this PR include:
- New binaries: eval-harness/bin/expectation_linter.py and eval-harness/bin/snapshot_summarizer.py
- A small CI adapter at .github/workflows/eval-lint-adapter.yaml that runs the linter and uploads the snapshot artifact
- New rule set schema: eval-harness/configs/eval_lint_rules.yaml with examples for prompt cohorts
- Tests: tests/expectation_linter_test.py and integration smoke test tests/ci_snapshot_endtoend.py
- Docs: docs/expectation-linter.md with usage, rule authoring guidance, and example failure screenshots
Migration notes: Default CI gate is a soft-fail for non-critical projects; teams can opt into hard-fail by adding the file .eval-lintrc at the repo root with {"fail_on": "hard"}. Linear link: ENG-7891 contains the prioritization and acceptance criteria. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for each rule type - [x] Integration smoke-run against a small seeded snapshot - [x] Docs and examples - [x] Telemetry hooks wired to the console exporter - [x] Backwards-compatible: existing eval invocations unaffected - [x] Performance: median overhead on CI runners measured at ~4s per 1k prompts
Implementation notes: The linter engine evaluates rules in a deterministic order and returns a ranked list of findings; each finding includes a severity (info/warn/error), affected examples (up to N=5), and an explanation string that includes the statistical test used. The summarizer computes compact delta vectors (median, 90th percentile, 95th percentile, and KL for categorical outputs) and tags tokens with saliency deltas when present. The CI adapter uses a three-tier gate: informational (post comment), soft-fail (annotate and continue), hard-fail (fail workflow). This PR wires the informational and soft-fail tiers; hard-fail is opt-in per team. Why this is different: Unlike prior PRs that focused either on single-metric thresholds or heavy snapshot replay systems, this combines a small, rule-driven linter with a compact summarizer and a CI-friendly adapter so teams get quick signal with low CI cost. Follow-ups: - Add model-aware baseline selection so rules prefer the nearest production model - UI: surface linter findings in Console under the 'eval-lint' tab - Add an autosuggest patch generator for common fixes (prompt edits, anchor reweighting)
commits: feat(ci): add snapshot summarizer and adapter
test: add unit and integration tests for linter and summarizer
docs: add expectation-linter guide and examples
chore: update CI matrix to include eval-lint job
review_comments: Claire Zhang: Nice separation of rule engine and summarizer; please add a short section in docs about interpreting KL numbers. Also add a test that simulates a tokenization shift.
Rajiv Menon: Added the KL explainer and a tokenization-shift fixture in tests/expectation_linter_test.py (commit 3).
Miguel Torres: CI job looks good but integration was flaky on the first run; moved the dataset seeding to before the job to stabilize.
Elena Petrova: Can we hook the summary artifact into the Console ingestion pipeline? Add a telemetry schema version header so we can iterate.
Rajiv Menon: Added telemetry schema header v1 and instrumented the console exporter (commit 4).
release_notes: Adds an expectation linter for eval metric distributions and a compact snapshot summarizer plus a CI adapter. Default gate is soft-fail; teams can opt into hard-fail. See docs/expectation-linter.md for usage and rule examples.
notes_for_oncall: This PR is low-risk but adds CI artifacts that the telemetry pipeline will ingest. If you see missing console events for 'eval-lint.v1.snapshot', confirm the pipeline auth token and that artifact upload from the CI runner is succeeding.
qa_steps:
1) Run `python -m eval-harness.bin.expectation_linter --rules eval-harness/configs/eval_lint_rules.yaml --input tests/fixtures/sample_prompts.json` and verify findings.json contains expected severities.
2) Run the CI adapter locally with `act` or in a dry-run workflow to confirm artifact creation.
3) Validate telemetry events appear in Console under eval-lint.v1 within 10 minutes.
impact_summary: Primary runtime impact is CI time (+~4s per 1k prompts measured); storage impact is small compressed snapshot artifacts (~50KB per 10k prompts). No runtime changes to the serving stack.
security_considerations: No new secrets; artifact uploads use existing CI credentials. The rules engine strictly reads local snapshots and does not execute arbitrary code. Added a schema validator to prevent malformed rule files from being applied.
team_signoff: Engineering: Claire Zhang, Miguel Torres. Product: Maya Lin.
